issues.failure_explanation: The operator d_h^Δ = Δ^i ∧ (S_i − id) is built from forward shifts, so it depends on the orientation of each lattice direction. For p=1 take n' = −n, which lies in GL(1,Z). The forward difference in n' uses S^{-1}, and d'f = (−Δ)(S^{-1}f − f) has coefficient f_n − f_{n−1}. The original operator has coefficient f_{n+1} − f_n, so the two differ. A shear n'^2 = n^1 + n^2 likewise changes the operator. Hence d_h^Δ is not invariant under all of GL(p,Z), contrary to the Remark.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the transformations that preserve the forward-difference structure (translations and coordinate permutations, or other maps preserving the lattice ordering), or state that d_h^Δ depends on the chosen orientation.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised full coordinate-free invariance of the difference bicomplex under lattice reparametrisations is overstated. No later formal result uses this invariance.
issues.title: Claimed GL(p,Z) invariance of the forward exterior difference is false
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of an unused remark suffices; no theorem or proof depends on the invariance.

issues.failure_explanation: The argument shows only that d_hη = d_vL on solutions, so E^Δ(L) = I^Δ(d_hη) = 0 on solutions. This says that solutions of the given system solve the Euler–Lagrange equations of L. It does not say the Euler–Lagrange equations are equivalent to the system. The paper itself notes in the differential case that the Euler–Lagrange equations of such an L may be weaker than the system. The text nevertheless claims an 'equivalent difference Lagrangian structure' and that L is 'a Lagrangian form for the system'.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The integrand in \eqref{eq:vehomo} is a smooth function of
closed form $\sigma$ is also vertically exact.

issues.failure_explanation: The complex Ω^{k,0} → Ω^{k,1} → … is claimed exact, including at Ω^{k,0}. The kernel of d_v on Ω^{k,0} consists of forms whose coefficients do not depend on u, which are not in the image of anything. The homotopy argument works only for l ≥ 1: the integrand is smooth at λ=0 'as l≥1', and the pull-back by scaling kills σ only when l ≥ 1. For l=0 the identity gives σ − σ|_{u=0}, not σ. So the proof establishes exactness only at Ω^{k,l} with l ≥ 1, and the columns are not augmented by the u-independent horizontal forms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State exactness for l ≥ 1 (equivalently, augment each column with the u-independent forms at the bottom) and add 'l≥1' to the corresponding sentence in Section 2.
issues.overall_effect: The statement, and the matching prose in Section 2 that every vertically closed form is vertically exact, is false for l=0. Later uses of vertical exactness (Hamiltonian, η, λ_ξ) are at l ≥ 1 and are unaffected.
issues.title: Vertical complex claimed exact at Ω^{k,0}, where it is not
issues.why_classification: A short local change to the statement suffices; the proof and all later uses already work for l ≥ 1.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof gets ker I^Δ = im d_h^Δ (exactness at Ω^{p,l}) from the difference version of (eq:ii). In Section 3 that version was itself derived from exactness of the difference bicomplex, which is what the appendix is meant to prove. Hence the key step is circular. The only independent tool is the homotopy identity (hohomo), asserted for all 1 ≤ k ≤ p. For k=p, d_hσ=0 for σ ∈ Ω^{p,l}, so the identity would give σ = d_h h^{p,l}(σ) for every σ. This is false: σ = d_vu∧vol has I(σ)=σ≠0 and is not d_h-exact. At k=p the identity needs an I^Δ term, and that top-degree identity (σ = I^Δ(σ) − d_h τ with explicit τ) is never established. The operators F and h_h are only asserted to satisfy (hohomo), with no verification.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the top-degree homotopy identity σ = I^Δ(σ) + d_h^Δ h_h^{p,l}(σ) directly from the stated F and h_h operators (a contained computation), or cite the exactness result at Ω^{p,l} from the literature. Restrict (hohomo) to k<p.
issues.overall_effect: Exactness of the augmented horizontal rows at Ω^{p,l}, i.e. the decomposition σ = I^Δ(σ) − d_h^Δτ used throughout the paper, is not proved.
